{{nihongo|'''Murayama Shrine'''|村山神社 (亀岡市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tanba Province]].

'''Murayama Shrine''' (むらやまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Mori, Shino-chō, {{ill|Kameoka, Kyoto|Q633996|qid=Q633996}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}. Its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== History ===
Founding is unknown for both honden and Hachiman-gū. Kiln remains such as Sue ware have been found on the plateau behind the precinct, and shards are also confirmed from the back mountain.

In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=register of deities}} of the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' completed in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), "Murayama Shrine" is listed in {{ill|Kuwada district|Q11537600|qid=Q11537600}} of Tanba Province, and ranked as {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}.

Shrine tradition says it once had vast shrine lands but burned in warfare; in {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} 27 ({{ill|1420|Q6209|qid=Q6209}}), Watanabe Rokurō Yorikata, administrator of Kokuon-ji who governed this area, restored shrine buildings, and around that time invited Hachiman-gū to stand alongside<ref>'Place Names of Kyoto Prefecture,' Murayama Shrine section.</ref>.

In {{ill|2017|Q25290|qid=Q25290}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 29), Hachiman-gū honden collapsed due to {{ill|Typhoon Lan (2017)|Q42108577|qid=Q42108577|lt=Typhoon 21}}<ref>[https://www.sankei.com/article/20180214-MTZP3UOMHFNCNGABYEAKXISHMA/ "Kyoto Prefecture subsidizes 12 undesignated cultural property repairs for typhoon damage, 4.83 million yen"] (Sankei Shimbun, Feb 14, 2018).</ref>.
